e: Auto Scaling across multiple AZs removes the single point of failure and scales with demand, and an RDS Multi-AZ deployment keeps a synchronously replicated standby that fails over automatically, so a server or power failure doesn't lose data. A single AZ, manual read-replica promotion, or self-managed databases leave gaps.

Kinesis Data Streams keeps records for 24 hours by default, but the application reads the data only every other day, so older records expire before they are consumed. Increasing the retention period (up to 365 days) fixes the data loss. More shards or the KPL don't extend retention.

Lambda functions should get permissions through an IAM execution role with the needed S3 permissions attached to the function. Resource policies control who can invoke the function, and embedding IAM user credentials is insecure.

Putting an SQS queue between S3 and Lambda buffers the upload events so a burst of documents isn't dropped, and Lambda polls the queue at a rate it can handle with retries. Timeout, replication, or a second function don't solve throttling or lost events.

A target tracking policy on CPU utilization scales the Auto Scaling group with demand during working hours, and scheduled scaling sets capacity to zero over weekends and restores it afterward, saving cost. ALB capacity and the internet gateway scale automatically and aren't managed by Auto Scaling.

The web servers' security group allows HTTPS (443) from 0.0.0.0/0, and the DB instance's security group allows MySQL (3306) only from the web servers' security group. Security groups only have allow rules (no deny), and allowing the whole subnet CIDR is broader than necessary.
Amazon FSx for Lustre is the fully managed Lustre file system that Lustre clients can mount. EFS doesn't support Lustre, and DataSync and Storage Gateway don't provide Lustre access.

Global Accelerator supports UDP and provides low latency and fast cross-Region failover, and an NLB handles UDP traffic for the ECS Fargate service that processes the data. ALBs don't support UDP, and Route 53 failover is slower because of DNS caching.

Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a highly available, durable SMB file share (Multi-AZ) that the Windows IIS servers can use, replacing the NAS share. RDS is a database, Storage Gateway still depends on on-premises storage, and EFS isn't supported on Windows.
Creating the EBS volumes as encrypted volumes ensures all data written to them is encrypted at rest. IAM roles, tags, or KMS key policies don't turn on volume encryption.

Aurora Serverless (MySQL-compatible) scales capacity up and down automatically for sporadic and unpredictable usage, so it's cost-effective, and it needs no database modifications. DynamoDB would require changes, and RDS or EC2-hosted MySQL cost more at idle.

S3 Block Public Access at the account level keeps all buckets and objects private, and an SCP that prevents changing the setting stops users from disabling it. The other options only detect or remediate after exposure, and RAM doesn't find public buckets.

Amazon SES is a managed email service that handles sending and deliverability, which removes delays and reduces the effort of fixing email delivery problems. SNS isn't built for marketing or transactional email, and EC2 email tiers add operational work.

An S3 File Gateway presents an SMB/NFS share to the business system, and the files written to it are uploaded to S3 in near real time, with minimal administration. DataSync on a daily schedule isn't near real time, and SFTP scripts or custom API automation add work.

S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between access tiers based on changing, unknown access patterns, with no retrieval charges and no analysis, which is the most operationally efficient. Per-object analysis, Glacier IR, or One Zone-IA don't suit unknown access patterns.

CloudFront caches static content (and accelerates dynamic content) near global users, and an RDS read replica offloads read traffic from the OLTP database, improving page load times. Redshift is for analytics, and Multi-AZ is for availability rather than performance.

A Compute Savings Plan covers both EC2 and Lambda usage and stays flexible as Lambda usage grows, and connecting the Lambda functions to the private subnet that contains the EC2 instances gives direct, low-latency access. EC2 Instance Savings Plans don't cover Lambda, and a public subnet or the Lambda service VPC don't give private access.

Adding the development account as a trusted principal in the production role's trust policy lets the dev users assume the role (with permissions granted in their dev IAM policy) and access only the production bucket, following least privilege and avoiding extra credentials. Administrator access or public buckets are too broad.

Setting EBS encryption by default in ap-southeast-2 makes new volumes automatically encrypted with minimal impact on employees, and an SCP attached to the root OU denying ec2:CreateVolume when ec2:Encrypted is false enforces it for all users, including the root user. Permission boundaries and IAM policies don't apply to every account's root user.

An RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster has two readable standbys, failover typically in under 35 seconds, and a reader endpoint to offload reads, with no extra read replicas to pay for. A Multi-AZ DB instance has a standby that can't serve reads and slower failover.

Transfer Family with an internet-facing VPC endpoint that has Elastic IP addresses and a security group limited to trusted IPs preserves the existing IP-based access, and EFS provides the shared, high-IOPS, POSIX storage while permissions are controlled per user. EBS can't be attached to Transfer Family, and S3 isn't as high IOPS.

SQS buffers the asynchronous requests, and ECS services that read from the queue can scale the service (and the cluster) based on queue size, handling large bursts. Containers can load the 1 GB model at startup, which fits better than Lambda, and idle models scale down when not used.

The JSON is an identity-based policy (it has no Principal element) that allows ssm:ListDocuments and ssm:GetDocument on all resources. Identity-based policies can be attached to IAM users, groups, and roles. Organizations take SCPs, and ECS and EC2 resources use resource policies or roles instead.

Reserved Instances give a discount for the steady 24/7 frontend nodes, while Spot Instances are the cheapest way to scale the short-lived, varying backend nodes. Spot isn't suitable for always-on frontend nodes, and Fargate costs more than Spot for flexible work.

gp3 lets you provision IOPS (up to 16,000) and throughput independently of storage size, and it is cheaper than gp2 and the provisioned IOPS io1/io2 types, so it fits 15,000 IOPS most cost-effectively. gp2 ties IOPS to volume size.
